Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematical Sciences is proposing to add a track in the existing Ph.D.
Mathematics degree.
Currently, there are two tracks, pure mathematics and applied mathematics.
The proposed track, mathematical statistics and probability, does not fit into either current track as it is a unique combination of pure and applied mathematics.
The new track reflects on the recently growing area of applications and theoretical development at the intersection of probability theory and statistics.
This unique blend between pure and applied mathematics, probability theory/applications and

2 mathematical statistics, makes this combination uniquely deserving a track in the Ph.D. program.
The proposed track targets the same audience as the mathematics department at our aspire to-be-like institution1, University of Connecticut, program, Ph.D. in Mathematics with thesis in Actuarial Science2.
Like, University of Connecticut’s track our proposed track is aimed at attracting students for employment in the financial area to work in industry e.g., brokerage, hedge funds, actuarial science, and insurance companies.
However, unlike University of Connecticut, our track needs to be more broad than focused, since many of our students we do attract are seeking employment in academia and almost all academic settings our students get employed are departments of mathematics and statistics.
Furthermore, we are a much smaller mathematics department than University of Connecticut and cannot create a too focused track.
According to the AMS classification of mathematics departments3, URI’s mathematics department is considered a small public math department.
We currently have 14 tenure-track faculty and 9 Ph.D. students.

Despite these small numbers, the faculty are highly productive, graduating 2-3 students on average per year4, but the number of graduate students has declined over the years from a high of 17 Ph.D. students in 2011-2012 to the current level of 9 students4.
This declined negatively impacts research.
This track is a much needed track aimed at attracting new graduate students (in line with URI 2016-2021 Academic Strategic Plan Goals 1 and 2 – see C1 Institutional Role) 5 and to further develop our growing area of probability, financial math, and actuarial science.

Why is the new program being developed?
The new track, mathematical statistics and probability, is filling in a gap in the Ph.D. program as a combination of pure mathematics and applied mathematics with additional benefit of application (applied skills) in areas that are highly desirable for employment (see B2a).
The new track focuses on the research area of the mathematical theory underlying statistical methods and their use; including probability theory, stochastic processes, Markov processes, and Banach spaces.
All of these areas are underlying structures in several new program endeavors at URI, actuarial science and data science.
These programs are not mutually exclusive.
URI cannot develop new programs at a research university without providing a research foundation.
The development of undergraduate degrees needs a strong, relevant foundational graduate programs to attract graduate students and researchers so that all programs can be cutting edge and move forward in this ever-changing modern world of mathematics.

In 2015, the faculty in the department developed a pre-actuarial program in conjunction with the College of Business which followed shortly afterwards with a tenure-track hire in financial mathematics to help foster the growth.
Since 2016, we worked on the development of the data science program and have been participating in research and curricula development and are also participating in the online graduate certificate in Data Science.
In 2018, we were given a position in probability theory to expand our current research program in this area.
Unfortunately, the faculty member resigned in 2020 – however we were reassured by Dean Riley that the position remains in the department and we will be searching in 2021.
By supporting this new track, URI would not only increase its much-needed graduate enrollment in mathematics and generate new revenue, but also establish itself as a provider of researchers in the area mathematical statistics and probability while growing and firmly establishing the building blocks of the actuarial science and data science programs.

In 1929, famous mathematician, Bertrand Russell stated, “Probability is the most important concept in modern science, especially, as nobody has the slightest notion what it means.” The importance of probability is even more true in this modern age with the need to predict and examine data.
We hope to change the notion that nobody understands what it means.

Shortly before the completion of formal course work, each doctoral candidate shall take the Ph.D. comprehensive examinations.

Seconded Motion: Add a new Section 11.10.17 to Chapter 11, Procedures for Changing the Manual. 11.10.17 Editorial changes to the University Manual are defined as and limited to changes requiredby developments in legal statutes or Collective Bargaining Agreements.
Whenever a determination ismade that editorial changes to a chapter or section of the University Manual are required outside theordinary maintenance schedule established in Section 11.10.16, based on developments in law or aCollective Bargaining Agreement, the interested party shall notify the Faculty Senate President andthe Faculty Senate Coordinator by providing a detailed justification for the request.

The Faculty SenatePresident will review the request with the Faculty Senate Executive Committee at their next regularlyscheduled meeting or refer the request directly to the Constitution, By-Laws and University ManualCommittee (CBUM).
Upon referral from the Faculty Senate President, CBUM members will review theproposal at their next regularly scheduled meeting or at a special meeting convened sooner than thenext regularly scheduled meeting, formulate a recommendation regarding approval, and present thechange request along with their recommendation in a report at the next regularly scheduled meetingof the Faculty Senate.

SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate NEW PROGRAMS: COLLEGE OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: School of Education: BA in World Language Education (All grades): The School of Education currently offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Secondary Education, with multiple tracks reflecting various specializations.
Since its inception, the World Language Education Program has been one of these tracks (the other tracks are English, History/Social Studies, Mathematics, and Science).
Upon graduation, students in the Secondary Education Program obtain certification to teach at the High School level (grades 7-12).

Upon the completion of an additional course and a teaching practicum at a Middle School, students in this existing program also have the option to obtain a Middle School extension, a credential that allows them to teach in grades 5-8 in any Rhode Island elementary, middle, or junior high school.
Recently the Rhode Island Department of Education changed the World Language teacher certification system.
Due to these changes, graduates from our current Secondary Education – World Language program are now certified to teach in Rhode Island at all levels of elementary, middle, and secondary education (grades PK-12).
The new program proposal is intended to address the changes in Rhode Island certification regulations, which will require significant changes (over 25%) to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into a BA in World Language Education-All Grades.

In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.
The new program will educate our students to become reflective teachers committed to global citizenship, social justice, and multicultural education.
Our program of study, based on current research and best practices, has been carefully crafted to provide our teacher candidates with ample opportunities to learn about different professional contexts and acquire knowledge about learning theory (social, emotional, and academic), and how to address the individualized needs of diverse learners.
Through a 1

variety of hands-on teaching experiences at PK-12 academic settings our candidates will have the opportunity to apply what they learn in URI courses in culturally responsive practices but also to learn to work with and from practicing teachers. The standard program of study that our candidates will follow will allow them to graduate from URI with a double major in Education and in a Foreign Language. Students will develop their teaching skills and acquire knowledge through coursework that focuses on teaching and learning at different developmental levels, and on cutting-edge second language acquisition theories. Our program will help teacher candidates develop the necessary confidence and experience to effectively engage with a diverse group of students in a variety of educational settings. Upon completion of our program and after successfully completing the licensure tests, our well prepared graduates will be ready to apply for the Rhode Island World Language teacher certification in grades K-12. 2

Explain and quantify the needs addressed by this program, and present evidence that the program fulfills these needs.
The School of Education currently offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Secondary Education, with multiple tracks reflecting various specializations.
Since its inception, the World Language Education Program has been one of these tracks (the other tracks are English, History/Social Studies, Mathematics, and Science).
Upon graduation, students in the Secondary Education Program obtain certification to teach at the High School level (grades 7-12).

Upon the completion of an additional course and a teaching practicum at a Middle School, students in this existing program also have the option to obtain a Middle School extension, a credential that allows them to teach in grades 5-8 in any Rhode Island elementary, middle, or junior high school.
Recently the Rhode Island Department of Education changed the World Language teacher certification system.
Due to these changes, graduates from our current Secondary Education – World Language program are now certified to teach in Rhode Island at all levels of elementary, middle, and secondary education (grades PK-12).
The new program proposal is intended to address the changes in Rhode Island certification regulations, which w ill require significant changes (over 25%) to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into a BA in World Language Education-All Grades.

In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.

One of the purposes of the new program is to attract, retain, and graduate more teachers from multicultural, multilingual, historically marginalized, and under -represented groups in the education profession.

The RIDE certification requirements for World Language teachers are:4 ● Bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution ● Completion of an approved program or Credential Review Consortium Institution (CRCI) credential review plan for the preparation of All Grades World Language Teachers in a specific language ● Completion of a minimum of 12 weeks of student teaching in this area and a minimum of 60 hours field experience prior to student teaching ● Demonstration of meeting the pedagogical competencies of the Rhode Island Professional Teaching Standards (RIPTS) ● Demonstration of meeting the content competencies as prescribed by the American Council for the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) Other requirements: ● Meet all Rhode Island pedagogy and subject matter testing requirements for this certificate area 4 See: <https://www.ride.ri.gov/Portals/0/Uploads/Documents/Teachers-and-Administrators-Excellent- Educators/Educator-Certification/Cert-Requirements/tbd_AG-World%20Languages-Req.pdf?ver=2015-01-22- 123036-823>.
The RIDE has stated that taking the PRAXIS II exam will not be a certification requirement in the near future.

12 Assessment Requirements: All applicants must meet the following Rhode Island assessment requirements: ● Applicants must achieve a passing score of 160 on the Praxis II Principals of Learning and Teaching – Grades K-6 Test (5622) OR a passing score of 157 on the Praxis II Principals of Learning and Teaching – Grades 7-12 test (5624) AND a passing score of 162 on the French World Language Test (5174), a passing score of 163 on the German World Language Test (5183), a passing score of 161 on the Latin Test (5601), a passing score of 168 on the Spanish World Language Test (5195), or a passing score of Advanced Low on all other world languages – Oral Proficiency Interview. ● Applicants prepared in a program where the language of instruction was not English must achieve a passing core of 64 on the Versant Pro Speaking and Writing English assessments.
